p=Path('docs/decisions/0009-ticket-assignment.md');p.write_text('''# 9. Ticket assignment

Status: Accepted

## Context

Agents need ownership of active tickets and notification when work is assigned to them.

## Decision

Every ticket carries a nullable assignee. Assignment uses a dedicated PUT endpoint and a store method, limited to active
states. Changes update the audit log and enqueue notifications together. Each actual assignment uses its audit sequence
in the notification key so pending assignments to different agents, or repeated later assignments, are never suppressed.
An identical assignee is a no-op. Unassigning sends no notification.

Data version 1 gains an optional assignee field: old records load as null. Raw CLI output appends assignee after its
existing four columns. Listing filters are conjunctive, including an explicit null filter for unassigned tickets.

## Consequences

Existing data and report column positions remain readable. A resolved or closed ticket retains its assignee but cannot
change it until reopened. Each assignment notification can be delivered and retried independently.
''')

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('package.json'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('"version": "1.4.0"','"version": "1.5.0"'))
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('# Changelog\n', '# Changelog\n\n## 1.5.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Atomic `POST /tickets/import` batches of up to 5000 tickets, with ordered ids, audit entries and requester notifications.\n- Imports save the complete batch once; invalid items report their zero-based index without changes.\n'))
p=Path('docs/api.md'); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace('### List tickets:', '''### Import tickets: `POST /tickets/import`

```json
{ "tickets": [ { "title": "VPN drops", "requester": "maria@example.com" } ] }
```

Accepts up to 5000 items, each with the same fields and validation as creating one ticket. Creates tickets in array
order and answers 201 with `{ "created": 1, "ids": ["T-0001"] }`. An empty array succeeds with no changes.
Every ticket gets its ordinary creation audit entry and outbox notification, using the request's `X-Actor`.
If any item is invalid, no tickets, audit entries or notifications are added, and no ids are consumed. The 400 `invalid`
message identifies the first invalid item by zero-based index, for example `tickets[0]: title must not be empty`.
Imports allow bodies up to 16 MiB (or `MAX_BODY_BYTES` when larger); other endpoints keep `MAX_BODY_BYTES`.
The entire batch is saved once before success is returned ([decision 9](decisions/0009-atomic-import.md)).

### List tickets:'''); p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('the largest request body accepted |', 'the largest ordinary request body accepted; imports allow at least 16 MiB |'))
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 9 | [Atomic ticket imports](0009-atomic-import.md) | Accepted |\n')
Path('docs/decisions/0009-atomic-import.md').write_text('''# 9. Atomic ticket imports

Status: Accepted

## Context

The old tracker migration needs to create up to 5000 tickets per request within ten seconds. Saving the entire growing
state after each ticket is too costly, and an invalid item must leave no changes.

## Decision

Validate every item in order with the existing new-ticket rules, reporting the first failure as `tickets[index]`.
The store stages a batch in a separate in-memory store, using ordinary creation for audit and outbox effects, saves
that complete state once, then publishes it. An empty batch changes nothing. The import endpoint accepts at least
16 MiB so 5000 valid tickets fit without changing the ordinary request limit.

## Consequences

An invalid batch consumes no ids and produces no effects. A persistence failure leaves the live store unchanged.
The existing persistence format and notification worker are reused. Staging requires a copy of the existing state
and the incoming tickets in memory while a batch is processed.
''')

p=Path('test/due.test.js');s=p.read_text().replace("{ status: 'in_progress' }", "{ to: 'in_progress' }").replace("{ status: 'resolved' }", "{ to: 'resolved' }").replace("{ status: 'closed' }", "{ to: 'closed' }");p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text().replace('| `PORT`', '| `DUE_TIMES` | off | `on` exposes persisted `due` times and enables the overdue filter |\n| `DUE_HOURS_URGENT` | `4` | response hours for new urgent tickets |\n| `DUE_HOURS_HIGH` | `24` | response hours for new high tickets |\n| `DUE_HOURS_NORMAL` | `72` | response hours for new normal tickets |\n| `DUE_HOURS_LOW` | `168` | response hours for new low tickets |\n| `PORT`',1);s += '\nDue hour settings are whole numbers from 1 to 876000. Due times are fixed at creation, even when priority or settings change.\nSee [the rollout procedure](docs/operations.md#due-times-rollout) before enabling them.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s += '\n## Due times\n\nWith `DUE_TIMES=on`, all ticket responses include `due`, an ISO timestamp fixed at creation.\n`GET /tickets?overdue=true` selects only open and in-progress tickets with `due` strictly earlier than the current time, before cursor pagination. Existing status and priority filters still apply with their existing semantics.\n`overdue=false` leaves the listing unrestricted; other values return 400. With due times disabled, the parameter is ignored and ticket responses retain their original shape.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s += '''
## Due times rollout

1. Back up `DATA_FILE`. Deploy 1.5.0 with `DUE_TIMES` unset and select the desired `DUE_HOURS_URGENT`, `DUE_HOURS_HIGH`, `DUE_HOURS_NORMAL`, and `DUE_HOURS_LOW` settings.
2. Start the service. Before accepting requests, it assigns missing due times from each ticket's own creation time and priority and atomically saves the file. Existing due times, audit, updated timestamps and outbox are retained. A save failure prevents startup. New tickets also receive persisted due times while the feature is hidden.
3. Inspect the saved file to confirm every ticket has `due`, then restart with `DUE_TIMES=on`. An in-memory deployment needs no migration file. Changing hours affects only future tickets; changing priority never changes an existing deadline.

To hide the feature again, restart without `DUE_TIMES=on`; stored deadlines are retained. To roll back the binary, stop 1.5.0 and start 1.4.0 on the same file. The format remains version 1 with additive ticket fields, so 1.4.0 loads every ticket, audit entry and outbox event. Its writer drops the unknown `due` field: if upgrading again after rollback writes, use the backup to recover original deadlines or accept recalculation for missing values. Only one process may write the file.

The CLI respects `DUE_TIMES=on`, shows due times in human output, supports `list --overdue`, and appends `due` after the four established raw columns. Weekly reports continue reading their original column positions. The CLI never saves or migrates files.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');s=p.read_text().replace('# Changelog','# Changelog\n\n## 1.5.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Persist fixed response deadlines with configurable priority hours and startup backfill.\n- Gate due responses and overdue listings with `DUE_TIMES=on`; retain version 1 data for rollback.\n- Show enabled deadlines in operator output, preserving the existing raw column positions.',1);p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/decisions/0009-persisted-due-times.md');p.write_text('''# 9. Persisted due times with staged exposure

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must survive priority edits and configuration changes. Production needs a data-first rollout and binary rollback to 1.4.0.

## Decision

Store an additive optional `due` timestamp on version 1 ticket records. Compute it once from creation and priority hours. Backfill missing values in the store at startup and atomically save before serving, regardless of the exposure flag. Migration changes no audit, notification or updated timestamp. Hide due fields and ignore the overdue query until `DUE_TIMES=on`. Overdue is a strict past deadline on open or in-progress tickets, applied before pagination alongside existing filters.

## Consequences

The previous reader ignores the added field and can load the whole file. Its writer drops unknown fields, so deadlines must be restored from backup or recalculated after rollback writes. Operators configure hours before migration and enable exposure after verifying the saved file.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s += '| 9 | [Persisted due times](0009-persisted-due-times.md) | Accepted |\n';p.write_text(s)
